key_insight: Microstructured copper electrodes can reduce electrolysis overpotential, but their added surface area must be balanced against bubble-induced blockage and transport losses.
engineering_relevance: Coupled bubble-flow and electrochemical modeling can guide electrode geometry design for more efficient alkaline hydrogen production.
method: Couple two-phase CFD with Butler–Volmer and Faradaic kinetics.
Model bubble effects on electrochemical surface area and overpotential.
Validate fabricated electrodes using polarization curves, cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy, and linear polarization resistance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports model deviations below 7% for electrochemical surface-area enhancement and 15% for overpotential, with experimental overpotential reductions of 2.49–21.39% for oxygen evolution and 9.55–24.32% for hydrogen evolution.
watch_item: Industrial scalability is proposed, but the abstract does not establish long-term durability or performance under industrial operating conditions.
paper_title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
